newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Christian churches hit racism.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Christian churches hit racism.

text.p: Australia's Christian church leaders united on Thursday to condemn the policies of race row politician Pauline Hanson, urging Australians not to give in to "voices that call forth racism and hate".

A letter from the National Council of Churches sent to all followers of Australia's 11 Christian churches appealed to parishioners to embrace ethnic diversity, support Aborigines and not blame migrants for the country's problems.
"Voices that call forth resentment, racism and hate are getting a hearing Australians normally would not give them," the letter said.
"In the present atmosphere, we who claim to be Christians, have a special responsibility to ensure our attitudes and involvements as citizens are informed by the faith we profess."
A church council official said the letter did not name Hanson because it was not aimed at her personally, but at her anti-immigration, anti-Aboriginal policies.
"Our primary concern is the socially harmful forces that are running just under the surface," the official said.
But Hanson, who a year ago was running a small-town fish and chip shop and is now ranked by polls as potentially Australia's third political force, told the churches to stick to the pulpit.
"I've always grown up to believe that churches should not be getting involved in politics," Hanson said in a radio interview.
"I am voted in as a politician to voice my opinion on the direction of the country and the people," he said.
"I don't delve into preaching to people, so I don't want the church to delve into politics."

Hanson has sparked a divisive national race row, warning Asians threaten to over-run Australia and claiming Aborigines received special treatment from the government at the expense of white Australians.
